answer: Free-space optical links across a canyon mitigate Sybil attacks through directional verification. Agents prove identity by aiming collimated lasers at detectors set in basalt, using opal diffraction filters to confirm beam arrival angles. Because each identity requires dedicated transceiver optics and motorized servos, attackers face unavoidable hardware and site installation costs. However, atmospheric turbulence and thermal haze scatter beams, causing sporadic verification dropouts.
